result.title: PathStream: Towards Streaming Diagnostic Copilots for Whole-Slide Pathology
result.summary: Pathologists reach a diagnosis by integrating morphological evidence across regions and magnifications along viewing trajectories. Existing pathology AI rarely reflects this process: models predict from selected image regions, answer questions within fixed visual contexts, or navigate slides autonomously. We formalize pathologist-led streaming diagnosis, in which the pathologist controls navigation while a copilot selectively describes incoming views and synthesizes accumulated evidence into a final diagnosis. We record five pathologists' viewing trajectories on 1,791 TCGA whole-slide images (WSIs) spanning ten organs, with response labels, morphological descriptions, and session-level findings and diagnoses. We construct PathStreamBench to assess response timing, morphological description, and session-level diagnosis, alongside auxiliary video understanding. We introduce PathStream, which jointly learns streaming responses and diagnosis through two-stage training, with a diagnosis-attention loss guiding attention during diagnosis to relevant visual and textual evidence accumulated as the examination unfolds. PathStream outperforms 14 vision-language models and three domain-fine-tuned baselines on the core tasks, achieving a trajectory WSI Relevance score of 77.87, surpassing the strongest domain-fine-tuned baseline's 62.76. Without additional training, its diagnostic capabilities generalize to new educational pathology videos, three external centers, and an unseen organ.

AI.brief_summary: 论文形式化“病理专家主导的流式诊断”，基于五位病理学家在 1,791 张 TCGA 全切片上的阅片轨迹构建 PathStreamBench，并提出两阶段训练的 PathStream，以诊断注意力损失把注意力引导到累积的视觉与文本证据上，联合学习流式响应与会话级诊断。
AI.relevance_reason: 阅片轨迹中的响应时机与证据累积直接对应 LOOK/STOP 决策与视觉证据筛选，可供核查其增量状态如何组织与更新；但状态以显式描述和图像视图承载，并非 latent 推理状态，与 LVR 内部表示的对应关系仍需阅读原文判断。
